justification: Contributes a reversibility formalism and an Earliest-Conflict Rollback rule fixing what the loop re-executes next; validated only on StreamBench in the lab, not in deployment.
Contribution is goal decomposition into an agent tree with control-flow nodes ordering subgoal execution; evaluated as a prototype on WAH-NL and ALFRED, so lab validation.
RAT's claim is the revise-each-thought-step loop after an initial CoT, i.e. the correction rather than the check; lab benchmarks on code, math, writing and embodied planning.
Headline artefact is an instrument: a four-paradigm categorisation plus system-level benchmarking of embodied agent workloads; all measurement is lab benchmarking, not field use.
Novelty is the iterative self-refinement round after an off-the-shelf PDDL validator judges the plan, so the correction is the object; success rates measured in simulated planning domains.
M3 contributes model selection and routing of subtasks across the agent's tool models, i.e. the arrangement itself; validated on the authors' MS-GQA dataset in the lab.
Contribution is a way of measuring loop behaviour - task length executable per turn and the self-conditioning effect - via designed conditions that supply plan and knowledge; lab only.
Grounded decoding selects the next action by combining LM likelihood with grounded objectives, determining what the loop does next; compared against baselines in simulation and lab robot domains.
VLP is a tree-search procedure expanding and selecting candidate video-language plans with a learned value function; compared to prior methods on simulated and lab robot platforms.
Statler's contribution is an explicit world-state estimate kept outside the history and read back to condition each action; prototype compared against Code-as-Policies on lab robot tasks.
The claimed mechanism is LLM checkers detecting syntactic and semantic errors in the translated task representation before TAMP consumes it; lab comparison against LLM-planner baselines.
VADER's mechanism detects execution errors and decides when to defer to a human or peer robot, an escalation gate; evidence is a lab pilot plus a user study with 19 participants.
Compares four centralized, decentralized and hybrid multi-robot communication architectures, i.e. the arrangement itself; varied scenarios and agent counts in simulation, never deployed.
AWM induces reusable workflows into a memory store and selectively retrieves them into later episodes, governing what carries across tasks; measured on Mind2Web and WebArena.

First stated contribution is the multi-agent architecture and asynchronous execution framework arranging generate-critique-rank agents; consequences studied in three real biomedical programmes with wet-lab validation.
DEPS contributes plan repair and a trainable goal selector that reorders candidate subgoals, deciding the loop's next step; lab benchmarks on Minecraft, ALFWorld and tabletop tasks.
TARV is a runtime monitor computing trust signals that validate actions, memory writes and messages during execution; evaluated in the authors' own multi-agent environment, not in production.
Contribution is a learned world model with transition-focused observation abstraction used to select the agent's next action; benchmarked on WebArena and Mind2Web in the lab.
The artefact is a diagnostic instrument locating failures across planning, execution and replanning layers; evidence is a designed PDDL-versus-natural-language plan comparison in the lab.
Web-Shepherd is a process reward model used as a step-level verifier gating web trajectories; validated on the authors' WebRewardBench and WebArena-lite, a lab setting.

Contributes an instrument for measuring multi-turn loop behaviour - a KL-divergence drift measure and recurrence dynamics - tested with reminder interventions on synthetic tasks and simulated tau-Bench users.
The named mechanism verifies task feasibility, monitors execution success and traces failure causes before recovery; success rates compared with prior methods across eight lab manipulation tasks.
Offers structural criteria for what counts as long-horizon - information-set closure, four non-closure sources, three-layer lower bounds - as a conceptual framework with no empirical method.
AgentCollab decides when to escalate to a stronger, costlier tier and how much extra reasoning budget to allocate from failure signals; measured on multi-step agent benchmarks in the lab.
REPL-Plan expresses the plan as code executed in a read-eval-print loop, so control flow, variables and functions fix the next step; compared with prior methods on planning benchmarks.
